topic: Claude of Duty: Building a Call of Duty-Quality FPS from a Single Prompt
keyword: Claude of Duty single prompt FPS game

key_points: Primary source — the project itself, created by Matt Shumer (mshumer)
1,084+ GitHub stars, 210 forks in just 3 days (July 25-28, 2026)
~55k lines of JavaScript across 11 subsystems, all AI-generated from a single prompt
Built with Three.js r180 and WebGL2, zero external art assets — all procedural

11 subsystems: render (HDR pipeline, CSM, TAA, bloom), materials (19 procedural surfaces), sky (atmospheric scattering), world (120x120m market street), physics (BVH, swept-capsule, ragdolls), player (movement state machine), weapons (procedural geometry, ballistics), fx (GPU particles, decals), ai (navmesh, cover behavior), ui (DOM/CSS HUD), audio (Web Audio synthesis)
Performance: 28-30 fps after optimization (was 12-17), 3.7-4.6s boot time
Honest self-assessment: 5.05/10 vs Call of Duty — critics always picked real CoD in blind A/B
Key weaknesses: blocky hands, procedural texture ceiling, mannequin-like characters, no real GI, 28-30 fps at Retina
Process insight: sequential single-owner passes beat parallel fan-out decisively

stats.fact: Claude of Duty generated ~55,000 lines of code across 11 subsystems from a single prompt
1,084+ GitHub stars and 210 forks within 3 days of creation (July 25-28, 2026)
Performance improved from 12-17 fps to 28-30 fps after optimization pass with zero visual change
Worst frame time reduced from 728-1236ms to 66-82ms after shader pre-warming
Shader compiles during gameplay eliminated from 34-35 to 0 via prewarm.js
11 adversarial critics scored frames 3.59 → 4.14 → 4.05 → 5.05 out of 10 against Call of Duty
Every critic in every round picked the real Call of Duty frame in blind A/B testing
Triangle count grew from 5.9M to 11.3M with art passes
Sequential single-owner passes improved score +1.00 and cut defects from 66 to 26, while parallel fan-out only moved +0.46 and left defects higher
Physics system: Binned-SAH BVH with 29k tris → 14k nodes in 22ms, 0.25 µs/raycast
World: ~120×120m market street with modular building kit, enterable interiors, several hundred instanced props
19 procedural PBR surfaces generated at load time: concrete, brick, plaster, asphalt, sand, various metals, wood, fabric, burlap, glass
Only runtime dependency is Three.js r180 — no external images, models, HDRIs, or audio files
